title: Minnahanonck (Roosevelt Island)
summary: Minnahanonck is connected with Blackwell's Island in the East River, the island now known as Roosevelt Island. The name appears in early New Netherland sources connected with Marychtenwikingh people from present-day Brooklyn.
history_content: Minnahanonck connects a Native-language form with East River island geography and later colonial documentation.
translation_content:
A recorded variant is Minnehanock. Tooker compares the Connecticut form Manhannock and explains the name as island place or land on the island.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are powerful. They carry meaning by reminding us that history has relevance in our own time.”

— California State University San Marcos Presidential Taskforce, Final Report: Naming of Craven Hall (2022), Introduction, PDF page 2
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: the pin is placed near the center of modern Roosevelt Island, historically Blackwell's Island, to represent the island placename; it is not an exact point for a historic landing or boundary.
